clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old man with mechanical aortic valve, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation presented with fever (38°C), mental confusion, hypotension (90/60 mmHg), tachycardia (115 bpm), and dehydration. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed cytopenias affecting two lineages (severe thrombocytopenia 30,000/μL and normochromic macrocytic anemia Hb 11.2 g/dL), acute kidney injury (BUN 159 mg/dL, creatinine 1.99 mg/dL), and markedly elevated LDH (2494 IU/L). Further workup demonstrated hyperferritinemia (2656 ng/mL), hypertriglyceridemia (343 mg/dL), and splenomegaly (15.5 cm on ultrasound). Bone marrow examination confirmed hemophagocytosis coexisting with atypical lymphoid cells (CD20+, MUM+, bcl-2+, bcl-6+, CD10-, Ki67 100%) consistent with an underlying lymphoproliferative trigger. Urine culture was positive for E. coli. HLH diagnosis was established based on fulfillment of 6/8 HLH-2004 criteria (fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperferritinemia, and hemophagocytosis on bone marrow). Despite immediate institution of targeted HLH therapy, the patient died immediately after diagnosis due to acute pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock.
